items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: it's an elephant which is back from the Connie Mack era when they were the Philadelphia Athletics.

ctx.x: So what inspires a melodic line for you? Where does it start?

I’m not sure where it starts. I mean I think there’s a couple different approaches that I use and one is melody based, you know where the first thing that you come up with is a melody that anybody could — you just have something in your head and it could be a fragment of something else you’d heard that day, it could be — it could come from anywhere. It could be oh I had MLB network on and they had this like goofball theme and like for some reason it stuck in my head and then two weeks later you have something…

melody in on top of that. And then kind of the third way would be dealing with the rhythmic element first and that’s going to create a different approach to how you’re going to write the melody. So I think I just kind of roll with whatever happens on that. The two tunes that you are referencing, “Life Lived” is a composition for six trombones that I wrote for a record I did called “New Brass.” And yeah, it’s exactly, it was a dedication to victims of 9/11. So you know that kind of has an implication about what…
